text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: *ALERT* `hosted-gateway` p95 latency regression
- Service: `inference-gateway`
- Env: `hosted-prod`
- Region: `us-east-1`
- Trigger: p95 latency > 2.5s for 10m (baseline ~650ms)
- Error rate: 1.2% (baseline ~0.2%)
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/llm-gw/hosted-gateway?var-region=us-east-1
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGSRE/LLM+Gateway+Latency

Rafael Mendes: On-call here. Acknowledged. Seeing it on the graph, started ~15-20m ago. Paging runtime + SRE lead. :eyes:

Neha Kapoor: Joining. What changed right before the spike? Deploy? config? capacity?

Allison Grant: Looking at event stream. There’s a `config-change` annotation on the dashboard at ~T-18m. Correlation id `cfgchg_7c2f...`.

Sean Gallagher: I’m in. Rafael, can you drop the top impacted routes/models? Also check if it’s global or just one tenant.

Rafael Mendes: Impact seems concentrated on `/v1/chat/completions` for `rwi-llama-3.1-70b` in `us-east-1`. p95 went from ~700ms -> 3.1s. qps steady. GPU util jumped and queue depth rising. Not seeing same in `eu-west-1`.

Aisha Bello: Error budget panel shows a burst of `429` + `context_deadline_exceeded` from gateway. Not a full outage but trending.

Mateo Alvarez: Runtime here. Anything in runtime deploys? I don’t see a rollout in the last hour for `runtime-worker`.

Rafael Mendes: No runtime deploys. Last deploy on gateway was ~3h ago, stable since. This really looks like an optimization knob flip.

Allison Grant: I pulled the control-plane audit feed (internal). There was an Optimize config apply for scope `hosted/us-east-1/default` around the start of the spike.

Sofia Ivanova: If batching got too aggressive, you’d see queueing + tail blowup exactly like this. Can you confirm current batching params?

Rafael Mendes: That’s the problem: I can’t see history cleanly in Console right now, only the current config blob. Trying to grep the config service logs.

Chloe Martin: Console backend here. For now, quickest path is to query `config-control` directly. I can run:
`rwctl optimize-config get --scope hosted/us-east-1/default --format yaml`

Dylan Brooks: +1. We do not have version history in UI yet (this is exactly the gap). Chloe, can you paste current values for the batching + cache toggles?

Chloe Martin: Current from `rwctl`:
- `continuous_batching.enabled: true`
- `continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens: 65536` (was 32768 historically iirc)
- `scheduler.max_concurrent_requests_per_gpu: 96`
- `kv_prefix_cache.enabled: true`
- `kv_prefix_cache.max_entries: 200000`
- `quantization_profile: int8_w8a16_v2`

Sofia Ivanova: max_batch_tokens 65536 + 96 concurrent smells risky for 70B on this traffic pattern (long contexts). This can absolutely nuke p95.

Mateo Alvarez: Agreed. Any chance the quant profile changed too? int8_w8a16_v2 should be ok but if kernels mismatch we might see retries.

Omar El-Sayed: If prefix cache max_entries got cranked, could be memory pressure + eviction churn. Also changing quant profile without warmup can spike first-token latency.

Neha Kapoor: We need immediate mitigation. What’s the fastest manual rollback path right now? Can we revert those knobs to the prior safe defaults?

Rafael Mendes: I can manually apply a new config with the old values, but it’s risky without knowing exactly what the previous was. No one-click rollback, no known-good pointer. :/

Sean Gallagher: For mitigation: prioritize restoring latency. Set conservative bounds and disable the risky bits if needed.
Proposal:
- set `max_batch_tokens` back to 32768
- reduce `max_concurrent_requests_per_gpu` to 64
- keep cache enabled but lower `max_entries` to 50000
- leave quant profile as-is (unless we see correctness errors)

Sofia Ivanova: +1. Also consider temporarily disabling continuous batching if queue keeps growing, but try the lower caps first.

Allison Grant: Adding note: we should post customer-facing status update once mitigation starts, since Dedicated tenants might be watching shared status feed.

Rafael Mendes: I’m going to push a manual config change via `rwctl optimize-config apply` to the above. Will tag correlation id in the incident doc.

Devon Price: deploy-bot can post the config apply event into this channel if you include `--notify incidents`. Want me to run it from the automation host?

Rafael Mendes: Yes please, Devon. I’m worried about fat-fingering. If you can run the apply with an idempotency token, do it.

Devon Price: Running:
`rwctl optimize-config apply --scope hosted/us-east-1/default --file /tmp/mitigation.yaml --reason "INC-3187 mitigate p95 regression" --notify incidents --idempotency-key inc-3187-mitig-1`

incident-bot: :information_source: Config change initiated
- Scope: `hosted/us-east-1/default`
- Actor: `deploy-bot (Devon Price)`
- Reason: `INC-3187 mitigate p95 regression`
- Correlation: `cfgapply_2a91...`

Mateo Alvarez: Watching runtime propagation. It’s eventually consistent; workers pick up within ~2-3m but can lag if busy.

Omar El-Sayed: If we reduce cache entries, may want to invalidate prefix cache to avoid weirdness? (but that can also spike). I’d avoid flushing unless errors persist.

Aisha Bello: Queue depth is starting to flatten. p95 is still high but trending down slightly.

Rafael Mendes: Seeing new config live on a subset of workers (based on worker logs). p95 down to ~1.9s after ~5m, error rate back to ~0.4%.

Sean Gallagher: Good. Keep monitoring for another 10-15m and confirm p99 isn’t still awful.

Allison Grant: Adding an annotation on Grafana for `cfgapply_2a91...`.

Neha Kapoor: Next steps: identify who/what applied the original risky config. We need to feed this into the Safe apply + rollback project as a concrete example.

Chloe Martin: I can dig in audit logs, but right now it’s spread across `config-control` logs + internal events. This is exactly why Security keeps asking for immutable audit + UI deep links.

Dylan Brooks: Capturing: incident caused by Optimize config change without safe-apply guardrails + no rollback-to-known-good.
Action items I’m logging for the project:
1) immutable version history per scope
2) “rollback to version” button (one click)
3) audit event with actor/reason/ticket
4) preflight validator should flag max_batch_tokens > 32768 for 70B hosted default

Sofia Ivanova: Also add: validator should consider context length distribution. us-east-1 default traffic has heavy long-context; max_batch_tokens 65536 is a trap.

Mateo Alvarez: And runtime needs atomic apply semantics; if half the fleet picks up new config and half doesn’t, tails get weird. We saw partial propagation here.

Rafael Mendes: Confirmed: p95 now ~820ms, p99 ~1.6s, error rate ~0.22%. Looks back within normal.

Sean Gallagher: Nice work. Let’s keep the incident open for 20m to ensure stability, then close with a postmortem stub.

Allison Grant: I’ll pull a quick timeline:
- Alert fired
- Found config-change annotation
- Manual mitigation config applied
This should be used in the PRD as motivation.

Neha Kapoor: +1. Also, we should add a metric/alert: “config apply without canary” and “apply that changes batching/quant knobs above safe thresholds”.

Devon Price: One more thought: incident-bot should post a rollback deep link when there’s a config-change event. Today we had nothing to click, just hunting.

Rafael Mendes: Exactly. This took too long. If we had rollback-to-prev-known-good, MTTR would have been minutes.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Health check update
- `inference-gateway` p95 back under threshold for 10m
- Alert auto-resolved

Sean Gallagher: Closing when we have the follow-ups logged. Rafael, please create the incident follow-up task + link this thread.

Rafael Mendes: Will do. Marking main cause as “Optimize config change (batching caps) applied to hosted us-east-1 default without guardrails; rollback required manual re-apply of conservative config”.
